headline: Meta is rolling out new AI tools to find ads that secretly point users toward illegal child abuse material.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: new announcement on 7 Oct; the figures are Meta's own and not checked.
importance_line: What changed: Meta is adding AI checks on where ads lead, which affects children who use its apps and the people who could be drawn to illegal content; the doubt is that these figures and tools are Meta's own claims, with no outside check reported.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, said on Wednesday 7 October it had acted against 33.2 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content in the first half of 2026, more than 97 percent of it found by its systems before users reported it. It matters because Meta is now checking where an ad sends users, not only what the ad shows, to catch ads that look harmless but lead to illegal content elsewhere.
notes: Full article read. Figures are Meta's own statements.
